definition: A model in which only a subset of parameters or pathways are active for any given input, in contrast to a dense model where all parameters participate in every computation.
details: Sparse architectures, such as mixture-of-experts models, allow scaling total parameter count without proportionally increasing the compute required per input.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Here is the short version: A model in which only a subset of parameters or pathways are active for any given input, in contrast to a dense model where all parameters participate in every computation. The part that makes it sing: Sparse architectures, such as mixture-of-experts models, allow scaling total parameter count without proportionally increasing the compute required per input. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Sparse Model — is what makes everything else possible.
